title: Saturation Playbook — Cluster Utilization Spotlight (Apr 20 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook-style export from the weekly utilization dashboard; goal is to capture the short-term mitigation options and quick diagnostics for cluster saturation across pools and regions. Unlike the daily exports that just dump numbers, this is meant to be prescriptive: what to do when a cluster hits sustained >85% average utilization for 6+ hours, and who to ping.

Context and when to use:
- Trigger: any cluster or pool with 95th percentile GPU occupancy > 92% on a rolling 6 hour window OR sustained queue depth growth over 15% day-over-day.
- Audience: infra on-call, cluster owners, and SREs supporting Dedicated provisioning.
- This doc is a snapshot + checklist for the incident window and for planning the next capacity increment.

Quick snapshot (aggregated from monitoring, sampled 2026-04-20 08:00 UTC):
Cluster,Pool,Region,AvgUtilPct,95pUtilPct,PeakSlotsUsed,AvailableSlots,HeadroomSlots
cluster-e7,train-small,us-west1,72,94,112,8,2
cluster-a3,serve-medium,us-east4,81,97,256,4,0
cluster-h2,burst,eu-west1,64,78,48,32,16
cluster-r1,serve-large,us-west1,88,99,480,0,-24

Notes on numbers above:
- cluster-r1 is the primary pain point: overall average is 88% but 95th reaches 99% with negative effective headroom when weighted by reserved slots (we show -24 to indicate overcommit by tenants + reserved cap).
- cluster-a3 shows extremely tight tail behavior (95p 97%). Many requests are latency-sensitive — high tail is causing retries and transient error rates.
- cluster-e7 has decent average but narrow headroom (2 slots) which makes it fragile to sudden spikes.

Immediate mitigations (0-4 hours):
1) Short-term model fallback: push a canary policy to route non-SLO-critical requests from cluster-r1 -> cluster-h2 (burst pool) with quantized model variant (int8) for 60 minute trial. Responsible: Lina (routing), Owner: Aisha. Target: 15:00 UTC today.
2) Emergency burst allocation: increase autoscale burst for cluster-h2 from 1 extra slot per minute to 4 for next 2 hours to absorb spillover from us-west. Responsible: SRE on-call (Jon).
3) Reduce background batch jobs: throttle training batch jobs tagged "low-priority" across us-west pools to 40% for 3 hours; plan: schedule patch via job-queue-controller. Jira: JIRA-INFRA-1284.
4) Temp quota bump for Dedicated tenants with SLA downgrades: use route-level cost controls to allow overflow to dedicated-reserve-2 for critical customers only. Owner: Marco.

Diagnostics to run (immediately):
- Confirm KV cache hit rates on cluster-r1 for large context models — cache churn can increase per-token load.
- Check request size distribution: are 95th percentile seq_len spikes matching the utilization spikes? If yes, consider prefix caching on hot sessions.
- Verify preemption logs for background jobs — accidental low-priority jobs can be starving serve pools.

Medium-term fixes (24-72 hours):
- Rebalance slot reservations: reduce static reservation for test-team on cluster-r1 by 10 slots after confirmation with team. Owner: infra capacity planning (Aisha).
- Add one additional 8xA10x node to us-west1 serve-large pool (cluster-r2 provisional); procurement/quotas tickets opened. Linked artifact: PR to infra-terraform.
- Implement a canary traffic-slicing rule in routing layer that proactively sends 5% of non-critical traffic to underutilized clusters during peak windows to stabilize tail.

Long-term (weeks to quarters):
- Capacity smoothing: implement forecast-driven pre-warm policy that spins up reserve nodes 20 minutes before predicted spike windows (based on historical daily patterns).
- Add per-model quantization profiles to optimizer so that safe int8 fallbacks can be auto-applied when headroom < 10%.
- Instrument model-level cost and error deltas so quality regressions from fallbacks are tracked in the console per prompt set.

Runbook checklist (for on-call):
- [ ] Acknowledge alert (alert channel: #infra-capacity)
- [ ] Capture 6-hour window metrics snapshot -> paste in incident thread
- [ ] Run immediate mitigations (one or more of items 1-4 above) and record timestamp
- [ ] If headroom remains <5% after mitigations for 60 minutes, escalate to capacity planning thread and open dedicated-reserve request

Communications template (paste into #infra-capacity):
"Cluster saturation alert: cluster-r1 (serve-large) exceeding tail capacity. Current 95p=99%, effective headroom -24 slots. Actions: throttled low-priority batches, routing canary to burst pool, increased burst autoscale. Owners: Aisha, Jon. ETA next update: +30m."

Post-incident notes to capture after stabilization:
- Exact time window when 95p crossed 95% and when tail returned to <80%
- Which mitigation(s) materially reduced queue depth (routing vs throttling vs burst)
- Any customer impact reports (errors/rate-limits) and correlated customer IDs

Appendix (small trending snippets):
- Weekly delta (us-west serve-large): avg 7-day utilization up 12% vs prior week, peak concurrency moved from 430 -> 480.
- Typical day pattern: two peak windows 09:00-11:30 UTC and 20:00-22:00 UTC for us-west serve pools.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Do we want to permanently decrease reserved-test-team capacity on cluster-r1? (need approval from Test Team lead).
- Are there uninstrumented background pipelines contributing to load spikes? (investigate job metadata ingestion).

Action items (owners and due dates):
- Lina: deploy routing canary policy (due 2026-04-20 15:00 UTC) — status: in_progress
- Jon: increase burst autoscale for cluster-h2 for short window and monitor (due 2026-04-20 14:30 UTC) — status: done
- Marco: prepare dedicated-reserve escalation if headroom not recovered within 2 hours (due 2026-04-20 16:00 UTC) — status: pending
- Aisha: open follow-up capacity request and run capacity rebalancing proposal (due 2026-04-23) — status: pending

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc light and actionable; link to full dashboard for raw CSVs and p95/p99 charts. When we stabilize, move a cleaned version to Confluence under /infra/capacity/playbooks.

End of snapshot.
